The parents overlook the possibility that the babysitter could have intended to do all the tasks that parents want babysitters to do. The way that the babysitter learned of these tasks is not relevant to deciding whether the babysitter actually intends to do them.

stimulus: Travel agent: Studies show that people who travel frequently normally earn substantially more money, enjoy more time with their family, and have better physical health than people who do not travel often. Traveling is often described as a pleasurable experience. It is wonderful to see that traveling also increases a person's quality of life.
question: The conclusion above is unwarranted because

choices.A: traveling might not itself be a pleasurable experience; instead, it might be done solely to earn more money, enjoy time with family, and have better physical health
choices.B: people who do not travel frequently often do not find traveling a pleasurable experience
choices.C: the travel agent erroneously assumes that earning more money, spending time with family, and having better physical health are the only things that increase a person's pleasure while not traveling
choices.D: people who have more money, time to spend with their families, and better phys-ical health are more likely to travel frequently
choices.E: travel agents are motivated by self-interest to persuade people to travel frequently

explanation: The best answer is D. This is a conclusion question. The travel agent is assuming that because people who travel frequently have better physical health, more money, and time to spend with their families, frequent travel has somehow caused these things to occur. In fact, it is at least feasible that having better physical health, more money, and time to spend with family makes it more likely that people will travel frequently.

stimulus: The elementary schools in district X began a new athletic program where students participated in school-sponsored sports at least three times per week. During this last school year, the number of obese students attending elementary schools in district X decreased substantially. Based on these figures, the district's superintendent decided that the new athletic program was more effectual in keeping children, at least while in elementary school, from being obese.
question: All of the following, if true, weaken the superin-tendent's conclusion EXCEPT:

choices.A: Over the last year, parents with obese children in district X began sending their children to special weekend camps designed to help children lose weight.
choices.B: During this last school year, the school cafeteria began serving fruit in place of candy bars and soda.
choices.C: Obesity, like other unhealthy conditions, can lead to decreased cardiovascular health, increased joint pain, and self-esteem problems.
choices.D: The government, during this last school year, began requiring monthly weigh-ins for obese children and parental counseling about proper nutrition.
choices.E: A large number of the obese children's conditions were caused by depression, which was greatly alleviated by installing psychiatrists in each elementary school in district X.

explanation: The best answer is C. This is an EXCEPT question. The superintendent makes the assumption that the new athletic program is responsible for lowering obesity rates in district X. Answer choices A, B, D, and E all give other explanations for why obesity rates in district X have decreased that have nothing to do with the new athletic program.

stimulus: The elementary schools in district X began a new athletic program where students participated in school-sponsored sports at least three times per week. During this last school year, the number of obese students attending elementary schools in district X decreased substantially. Based on these figures, the district's superintendent decided that the new athletic program was more effectual in keeping children, at least while in elementary school, from being obese.
question: The superintendent's conclusion is more strongly supported if which of the following groups of students did not stop being obese during this last school year?

choices.A: obese students who participated in school-sponsored sports every day during the school year
choices.B: obese students who attended middle schools in district X that participated in the new athletic program
choices.C: obese students who participated in professional diet programs that encouraged frequent snacking
choices.D: obese students who actually gained weight during the school year, but lost weight during summer vacation
choices.E: obese students who had physicians write letters excusing the students from participation in the new athletic program

explanation: The best answer is E. This is a strengthen question. Because the superintendent concludes that the new athletic program has been responsible for lowering obesity rates in district X, this conclusion would be most supported by showing that obese children in the elementary schools who did not participate in the new athletic program did not stop being obese. Answer choices A and D actually weaken the superintendent's conclusion by showing that the new athletic program may not have contributed to lowered rates of obesity. Answer choices B and C do not support or weaken the superintendent's conclusion.

stimulus: Police officer: Traffic on major highways has been sluggish due to increased cell phone use while driving. Cell phone use while driving causes drivers to drive under the speed limit and to cause other drivers to pass them on the road. Drivers argue that talking on cell phones is necessary to discuss plans and ask directions and that traffic delays are inevitable. However, in Denton, the local officials have created a special lane for drivers talking on cell phones. This prevents these drivers from slowing down the rest of traffic on the highway. Therefore, it is possible to allow people to make plans and find out how to get to their destinations without causing sluggish traffic.
question: The police officer's argument proceeds by

choices.A: proposing an alternative method for drivers to discuss their plans and ask directions
choices.B: producing a counterexample to a general assertion
choices.C: questioning the motive of the drivers who maintain that traffic delays are inevitable
choices.D: pointing out a dissimilarity between drivers who talk on cell phones while driving and drivers in Denton
choices.E: appealing to the police officer's training on highway safety to discredit a commonly held view

explanation: The best answer is B. This is a method of argument question. The drivers are claiming that sluggish traffic is inevitable because people need to be able to make plans and find out how to get to their destinations by talking on their cell phones while driving. The police officer shows how Denton has managed to allow drivers to conduct their affairs while driving and still prevent traffic from being sluggish due to cell phone use by drivers. Answer choice A is incorrect because the police officer does not suggest an alternative method for discussing affairs or asking directions, but points out that Denton has established special lanes for these drivers that will prevent traffic from being sluggish.

stimulus: Increasing Mary's allowance would cause her to become spoiled and harm her chances of making new friends. Since Mary's parents would not do anything to cause their daughter to be unable to make new friends, they will not increase Mary's allowance.
question: Which of the following patterns of reasoning is most similar to that in the paragraph above?

choices.A: Older children function less well at earlier hours than younger children. Therefore, it makes more sense to have the elementary school students start earlier than high school students because this may lead to increased productivity.
choices.B: Children who attend schools with diverse populations are more likely to participate in community service projects. Since diverse populations in schools lead to increased community service participation, then all schools should have diverse populations.
choices.C: In school districts that use standardized tests, student achievement is lower than in other districts. Therefore, eliminating standardized tests will increase student achievements in these districts.
choices.D: If the new budget does not pass this election, a new school cannot be built to alleviate the overcrowding at the existing school. Voters will not continue to tolerate overcrowding at the existing school so the new budget will pass.
choices.E: The new school principle will probably not lower the teachers' salaries as this would create animosity among the staff and will cause him to be unpopular with his co-workers.

explanation: The best answer is D. This is a parallel question. "Increasing Mary's allowance would cause her to become spoiled and harm her chances of making new friends" is equivalent to "If the new budget does not pass this election, a new school cannot be built to alleviate the overcrowding at the existing school." "Since Mary's parents would not do anything to cause their daughter to be unable to make new friends" is also equivalent to "Voters will not continue to tolerate overcrowding at the existing school", and "they will not increase Mary's allowance" is most like "so the new budget will pass."

stimulus: Ethicist: In a recent judicial decision, a woman was ordered to pay restitution to her husband because of their recent divorce, even though the couple had signed a written prenuptial agreement prior to getting married which stated that each party would be financially independent and not seek alimony should the couple decide to divorce. Thus, it was morally wrong for the man to change his mind and seek restitu-tion.
question: Which one of the following principles, if valid, most helps to justify the ethicist's reasoning?

choices.A: It is morally wrong to seek a penalty for an action for which the agent is unable to make restitution.
choices.B: It is morally wrong to ignore the terms of an agreement that was freely undertaken only if there is clear evidence that the agreement was legally permissible.
choices.C: It is morally wrong for one party not to abide by its part of an agreement only if the other party abides by its part of the agreement.
choices.D: It is morally wrong to seek compensation for an action performed in the context of a promise to forego such compensation.
choices.E: It is morally wrong for one person to seek to penalize another person for an action that the first person induced the other person to perform.

explanation: The best answer is D. This is a principle question. The situation described in the stimulus is most closely analogous to the principle identified in answer choice D. The stimulus states that it is morally wrong for the husband to seek restitution, or compensation, when he had agreed not to do so in the event of a divorce, or in the context of a promise to forego such compensation. The other answer choices are incorrect because they state a context for the conclusion that does not match the context of the stimulus.

stimulus: Television commercial: Compared to other television cable services, Acme is clearly superior. Around the nation, thousands of satisfied Acme customers have testified on Acme's website that they have had uninter-rupted cable service for two or more years. Some of these Acme customers even testify that they have had uninterrupted cable service for five years! Obviously, if you sign up for Acme television cable service, you can be assured that you will have uninter-rupted cable service for years at a time.
question: The television commercial's reasoning is most susceptible to criticism on which of the following grounds?

choices.A: The commercial simply reiterates one of its premises and claims that it is a conclusion.
choices.B: The commercial incorrectly uses a key term to conceal the terms' innate ambiguities.
choices.C: The commercial bases its argument on premises that are inherently self-contradictory.
choices.D: The commercial makes a broad conclusion based on a few choice circumstances that may, or may not, be representative.
choices.E: The commercial bases its conclusion on the opinions of a few to show that the opinion is held by all.

explanation: The best answer is D. This is a flaw question. The fact that some of Acme's consumers testify to uninterrupted service on Local's website does not imply that all of Local's customers will have uninterrupted service as the television commer-cial suggests.

stimulus: Due to slow sales in the recent months, Bigger Box Company's president has decided to decrease the amount of money that the company spends to fund the factory workers' cafeteria from $200,000 per year to only $120,000 in the coming year. However, the factory workers' cafeteria is unable to continue serving meals with less than $180,000 per year. As the Bigger Box Company has flatly refused to give any more than $120,000 this year to the factory workers' cafeteria, the cafeteria will not be serving meals this year.
question: This conclusion is correctly drawn if which of the following is assumed?

choices.A: The factory workers' cafeteria will not receive the additional funding it needs to operate from any other source.
choices.B: The Bigger Box Company would go out of business if it gave more than $120,000 this year to fund the factory workers' cafeteria.
choices.C: The Bigger Box Company is aware that the factory workers' cafeteria will be unable to serve meals if it does not receive at least $180,000 in funding this year.
choices.D: The Bigger Box Company will also be cutting funding to other employee benefit and compensation programs.
choices.E: The Bigger Box Company will be unwilling to give more than $120,000 per year whenever sales have been slow for several months.

explanation: The best answer is A. This is a conclusion question. Because of Bigger Box Company's president's decision to decrease the funding to the cafeteria, it appears as if the cafeteria needs $60,000 to be able to serve meals this year. If the cafeteria can obtain that money from another source besides Bigger Box Company itself, the cafeteria will be able to serve meals next year. Answer choice B is incorrect because the conclusion that the cafeteria will not be serving meals this year does not depend on Bigger Box Company going out of business if it gave more than $120,000 to fund the cafeteria.

stimulus: The State has proposed a plan requiring all young people to perform community service as a requirement for graduation from high school. The goal is to use the young people to provide services to correct social ills, especially those in housing and crime. Young people, however, should only be required to participate in educa-tional activities to graduate from high school. For that reason, the proposed program should not be implemented.
question: Which one of the following is an assumption on which the argument depends?

choices.A: Community service is not beneficial to young people.
choices.B: Community service does not provide any educational benefit to young people.
choices.C: Young people cannot be motivated to help their communities.
choices.D: Some of the social ills that could be helped are being ignored by this program.
choices.E: Young people do not cause the social ills mentioned.

explanation: The best answer is B. This is an assumption question. The argument assumes that young people should not be required to perform community service because they should only be required to participate in educational activities. Therefore, the argument assumes that community service is not an educational activity.

stimulus: Lake salmon spawn only in the waters in which they were hatched. After being born, they leave the waters in which they were hatched and head out into the open water. After 10 years, they come back to spawn where they were born. It has been hypothesized that salmon can smell their birth environment, and it is this smell that stimu-lates the salmon to return to their birthplace.
question: Which only of the following, if true, would cast the most serious doubt on the hypothesis in the passage?

choices.A: Salmon have a very weak sense of smell and generally cannot smell any scent that is more than 10 feet away from them.
choices.B: Waters in which salmon spawn tend to be very cold.
choices.C: Salmon do not always live long enough to make it back to their birthplaces.
choices.D: Unlike other fish, salmon have a well-developed sense of sight.
choices.E: Salmon do not survive after they have made their return trip to their birth environment.

explanation: The best answer is A. This is a weaken question. If salmon have a weak sense of smell, then it is unlikely that they could use their sense of smell to direct them back from open waters to their place of birth. The other answer choices are irrele-vant to the question.

stimulus: The most common amphibian in the Tropicalico jungle is a unique variety of tree frog, but this variety is almost never seen, even by trained researchers studying the amphibian. Surprisingly, this frog is seen even less than tinier and less populous amphibian varieties, possibly less than any other amphibian type within the jungle.
question: Each of the following, if true, helps to reconcile the statements above EXCEPT:

choices.A: While many varieties of jungle amphibian will frequently move from plant to plant, the tree frog will often stay on the same tree for hours at a time without moving.
choices.B: Several jungle amphibians seek food during the day, but the tree frog is active only during dusk and dawn.
choices.C: Most amphibians in the Tropicalico jungle exhibit some sort of communal behavior and often gather around common water sources, but the tree frog takes in water through its skin so it has no need to congregate near a water source.
choices.D: Almost all of the trees within the Tropicalico jungle are covered in vines that bear a remarkable similarity to the patterns on the skin of the tree frog.
choices.E: The tree frog's croak is high-pitched and clearly identifiable while the croaks of most other frogs are low-pitched and indistinguishable.

explanation: The best answer is E. This is an EXCEPT question. The argument suggests that although the tree frog is very common, it is rarely seen. Many things could explain this, such as its stationary behavior, the fact that it is nocturnal, its ability to take water through its skin so as to avoid finding a water source, or its natural camou-flage. Answer choices A, B, C, and D are examples of such things. Answer choice E, however, is an example of a reason as to why the tree frog might be seen more often than is stated in the argument, and therefore does nothing to explain the paradox.

stimulus: Advertisement: Attention homeowners! All the pests in your yard will die within minutes of being treated by JTE pesticide. What's better, JTE pesticide is not harmful to the birds or small animals that make your yard their home. By using JTE, you can elimi-nate the pests in your yard and keep the rabbits and birds.
question: Which one of the following is an assumption on which the argument depends?

choices.A: JTE has met all state and federal environmental standards.
choices.B: JTE pesticide will not harm the plants in your yard that you want to keep.
choices.C: JTE pesticide will not harm the under-ground water supply.
choices.D: The rabbits, birds, or other small animals are not in your yard because of the pests.
choices.E: The effectiveness of JTE pesticide does not depend on the strict adherence to specific application procedures.

explanation: The best answer is D. This is an assumption question. The author of the argu-ment must be assuming that, given the statement that JTE can eliminate the pests yet keep the rabbits and birds, the rabbits and birds are not in your yard because of the pests (answer choice D). Since JTE will kill all the pests within minutes, and is not harmful to rabbits or birds, it relies upon the assumption that such animals do not see the pests as a food source. The potential that the birds and rabbits would leave if their food source was removed is countered by this assumption.

stimulus: Physician: To the extent that AIDS deaths occur from a lack of experimental medica-tions, it should not be inferred that such deaths are the result of ignorance. Governments will normally provide medica-tions if they believe such medications are helpful; it is impractical to suppose that governments will be willing to potentially waste their limited funds on medication unless they know the medication will lead to cures.
question: Which one of the following most accurately describes the role played in the physician's argu-ment by the phrase "to the extent that the rate of AIDS deaths occurs from lack of experimental medication"?

choices.A: It proposes a potential answer for the problem of AIDS deaths.
choices.B: It offers a conclusion to be argued for.
choices.C: It is presented as evidence necessary to sustain the argument's conclusion.
choices.D: It restricts the application of the argument to a part of the situation.
choices.E: It suggests that the primary cause of AIDS death is ignorance.

explanation: The best answer is D. This is a role of fact question. By using this introductory phrase, the physician is narrowing his discussion to only those AIDS deaths that occur from a lack of experimental medications.

stimulus: The faculty of Grey County Public Schools will shortly go on strike unless the school board increases their salary. As the school board presi-dent is well aware, however, in order to increase the faculty's salary, Grey County Public Schools would have to cut some of its after-school programs. So, some of Grey County Public Schools' after-school programs will be cut.
question: The conclusion above is properly drawn if which one of the following is assumed?

choices.A: The school board will refuse to increase the faculty's salary.
choices.B: The school board president has the authority to offer the faculty their desired salary increase.
choices.C: The faculty of Grey County Public Schools will not be going on strike.
choices.D: The faculty of Grey County Public Schools will not accept a package of improved benefits in place of their desired wage increase.
choices.E: Grey County Public Schools will begin to suffer from a lack of state funding.

explanation: The best answer is C. This is an assumption question. The argument proceeds such that the faculty will strike if they do not get their wage increase, and the only way to give them that wage increase is to cut certain after-school programs. The only way that one can be sure that certain after-school programs will be cut is if they rely on the assumption that the faculty does not strike—thus implying that they got their wage increase and that programs had to be cut to do so. The other answer choices are either irrelevant or contrary to the conclusion drawn.

stimulus: The majority of people in city Y spend an increasing amount of money on exercise equip-ment after they graduate from high school. For almost all of the people in city Y, the proportion of their income spent on exercise equipment remains consistent throughout their lives.
question: The statements in the paragraph above, if true, most strongly support which of the following conclusions about people in city Y?

choices.A: People in city Y tend to buy different types of exercise equipment after they graduate from high school.
choices.B: As people in city Y grow older, they spend more time exercising than they did when they were younger.
choices.C: People in city Y generally spend more on exercise equipment than they do on other luxury items.
choices.D: People in city Y spend more on exercise equipment than people in neighboring cities.
choices.E: People in city Y normally have greater incomes than they did prior to graduating from high school.

explanation: The best answer is E. This is a conclusion question. If people in city Y have greater incomes after they graduate from high school, then it is possible to see how they might spend more money on exercise equipment without spending a greater percentage of their income on the equipment.

stimulus: In 2006, hospitals in state W treated over 200,000 people for secondhand smoking–related diseases. These 200,000 patients cost healthcare insurance companies over $20 million. Over 120,000 people with these secondhand smoking–related diseases died in 2006 in state W. Many new smokers take up the habit yearly. Politicians in the legislature have suggested a bill that would require all smokers to pay small premiums to all the major healthcare insurance companies to cover the cost of treating people with secondhand-smoking diseases.
question: Which of the following statements, if true, support the politicians' proposed bill?

choices.A: The 200,000 people treated in 2006 for secondhand smoking–related diseases were each insured by one of the major health-care insurance companies.
choices.B: Treating people for secondhand smoking–related diseases is not more costly than treating diseases caused by smoking.
choices.C: Of the 120,000 people who died of second-hand smoking related diseases in 2006, none of them had health insurance.
choices.D: People most commonly are exposed to secondhand smoke at bars and restaurants.
choices.E: New smokers are more likely to expose others to secondhand smoke.

explanation: The best answer is A. This is a strengthen question. If the patients being treated for these secondhand smoke–related diseases were all insured by the same health-care insurance companies that would benefit from the bill, then the bill's logic is sound. Answer choice C is incorrect because it weakens the argument.

stimulus: It would be erroneous to assume that an employee is embezzling funds if there is no other evidence than the fact that the employee has a high balance on his company credit card. It is important to remember that embezzling only happens if the employee is using his company credit card for purposes other than to entertain clients.
question: The reasoning of which of the following is most parallel to that in the paragraph above?

choices.A: Most people who appear to be physically fit are not actually physically fit because being slender is not the only sign of physical fitness.
choices.B: Water purifiers should be used in areas where there are large quantities of iron in the water, but bottled water should never be drunk because it does not normally contain fluoride.
choices.C: Even if a small child is cranky, this does not necessarily mean that he or she needs discipline, because discipline is needed when a child is cranky and will not take a nap.
choices.D: Although some outdoor cats need food provided by their owners, most outdoor cats do not because they are capable of catching their own food.
choices.E: A child cannot be diagnosed with asthma just because he or she becomes out of breath quickly, because most children are simply out of shape.

explanation: The best answer is C. This is a parallel question. "It would be erroneous to assume that an employee is embezzling funds if there is no other evidence than the fact that the employee has a high balance on his company credit card." This is equivalent to saying that, "Even if a small child is cranky, this does not necessarily mean that he or she needs discipline." "It is important to remember that embez-zling only happens if the employee is using his company credit card for purposes other than to entertain clients." This is also equivalent to, "because discipline is needed when a child is cranky and will not take a nap." The paragraph and the statements in answer choice C both require something additional to what has been stated before a conclusion can be drawn. In the paragraph, the employee must also not be using his company credit card to entertain clients. In answer choice C, the child needs to be unwilling to take a nap before he requires disciplining.

stimulus: Zoologist: It is true that over the past 15 years, there has been a fourfold increase in government funding to preserve endan-gered species, while the number of endan-gered species needing such preservation has increased by only 70% (there were, however, a large number of endangered species to begin with 15 years ago). Taking into account inflation, the amount of funding is at least double what it was 15 years ago. Nevertheless, the current amount of funding from the government for species preservation is inadequate and must be enhanced.
question: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to reconcile the zoologist's conclusion with the above evidence?

choices.A: Over the past 15 years, the salaries of conservationists employed by the government to work on species preservation solutions have increased at a rate twice that of inflation.
choices.B: Unlike today, funding for the preservation of species was essentially nonexistent 15 years ago.
choices.C: The two government agencies responsible for species preservation are typically under budget and are known for an utter lack of cooperation.
choices.D: Within the past 15 years, there have been breakthroughs in species demography that allow scientists to identify those species most in need of protection far before they face any real risk of extinction.
choices.E: Compared to 15 years ago, many more individuals are focused on saving endangered species.

explanation: The best answer is B. This is a paradox question. If the funding available for species preservation was almost nothing 15 years ago, no matter how many times over it has increased, it will still not be sufficient. Most of the other answer choices are reasons for decreasing funding, or reasons as to why the funding is currently adequate. Phrases such as fourfold and at least doubled are tricky in that they can mask the true change in real terms of whatever variable is being measured.

stimulus: Biologist: The claim that there are a large number of shark attacks along the Gulf coast is false, for this claim is based upon the large number of newspaper articles about shark attacks. But because there are actually very few shark attacks, newspapers are more likely to print stories about them.
question: The biologist's argument is flawed because it

choices.A: assumes without warrant that the news-paper stories in question are not biased
choices.B: mistakes a property of each member of a group taken as an individual for a property of the group taken as a whole
choices.C: uncritically draws an inference from what has been true in the past to what will be true in the future
choices.D: presupposes the truth of the conclusion it is attempting to establish
choices.E: presupposes that most newspaper stories are about shark attacks

explanation: The best answer is D. This is a flaw question. The biologist bases his argument on an opinion that he already holds; there are very few shark attacks. This reasoning is flawed because it follows directly from the assumed truth of his opinion; it is circular logic to say that something does not happen often just because it is covered in the paper, when it is only covered in the paper because it does not happen often.

stimulus:
Leslie: I enjoy P's movies, but he should not be deemed a fabulous actor. Despite how memorable his performances have been, the plots in his movies have not been diverse enough to show a real range of talent.

Molly: You are incorrect in your assessment of what makes a fabulous actor. A fabulous actor does not have to appear in movies with greatly varied plots. But, a fabulous actor must, at a minimum, be able to master a specific genre of film.
question: Which of the following is the disagreement between Leslie and Molly?

choices.A: whether there are other prerequisites to becoming a fabulous actor besides giving memorable performances and appearing in movies with greatly varied plots
choices.B: whether all actors who give memorable performances are fabulous actors
choices.C: whether an actor needs memorable performances to be deemed a fabulous actor
choices.D: whether P has appeared in movies with greatly varied plots
choices.E: whether appearing in movies with diverse plots is necessary to be a fabulous actor

explanation: The best answer is E. This is a point of contention question. Leslie states that P should not be deemed a fabulous actor despite his memorable performances because the plots in the movies he has been in are not diverse. Molly argues that a fabulous actor does not have to appear in movies with greatly varied plots.

stimulus:
Linda: During the summer months, people normally take vacations. Therefore, during the summer months, the local economy suffers since local residents spend their money at their vacation destinations.

Billy: Why do you think that the local economy would be suffering? During the summer months, tourists who come to our city actu-ally spend lots of money at local businesses, attractions, and restaurants.
question: Which of the following most correctly explains how Billy's reply is related to Linda's argument?

choices.A: The reply offers an additional factor to consider that weakens Linda's conclusion.
choices.B: The reply shows that Linda fails to realize that people often are forced by their employers to take their vacations in the summer.
choices.C: The reply demonstrates that Linda fails to understand the economic effects of supply and demand and how they relate to the local economy.
choices.D: The reply argues that Linda's conclusion is correct, but not because of the reasons that Linda claims.
choices.E: The reply offers another reason why the local economy suffers during the summer months that is unrelated to vacations.

explanation: The best answer is A. This is a method of argument question. Billy is offering a reason why people taking vacations during the summer months do not cause the local economy to suffer. Billy is trying to show that Linda had not considered the possibility that people from other areas would take vacations in her town and spend the money that the residents on vacation were not spending in the town.

stimulus: A new type of shaving cream has gotten excellent reviews, but there is a worry that an ingredient in the cream can cause a severe allergic reaction. If consumers test the product on a small area of skin before using it, however, a painful allergic reaction can certainly be prevented. Therefore, the fear of the cream causing allergic reactions is completely unfounded.
question: The argument depends on which one of the following assumptions?

choices.A: The shaving cream will come with a money-back guarantee if consumers find they are allergic to it.
choices.B: The shaving cream can be tested on any area of the body, including the face.
choices.C: None of the consumers who have yet to use the shaving cream are allergic to it.
choices.D: The shaving cream may also contribute to increased sensitivity to sunlight.
choices.E: All consumers of the shaving cream will test the product on a small area of skin before using it.

explanation: The best answer is E. This is an assumption question. The author of the para-graph says that the fear of an allergic reaction is unfounded, but if consumers do not test the product on a small area of skin before using it, they still might have a severe allergic reaction. Answer choices A, B, C, and D are incorrect because the author's conclusion that there is no longer reason to fear allergic reactions does not depend on these statements being true.

stimulus: The most prestigious attorneys in law firm X are the ones who have shown the greatest ability to win cases. However, every year for the past five years, the average number of cases won by the most prestigious attorneys in law firm X has not been greater than the average cases won by the lower ranking attorneys.
question: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy?

choices.A: Law firm X has a policy of giving the cases that will be most difficult to win to the prestigious attorneys.
choices.B: None of the lower-ranking attorneys work on their cases with law firm X's prestigious attorneys.
choices.C: Normally, it takes at least seven years for a new attorney at law firm X to be considered a prestigious attorney.
choices.D: The more prestigious an attorney is at law firm X, the more likely that he or she will become a senior partner.
choices.E: All of the cases taken by law firm X deal with patent infringement or intellectual property.

explanation: The best answer is A. This is a paradox question. Answer choice A is correct because this would explain why attorneys who have a greater ability to win cases are nonetheless only winning the same amount of cases as the lower ranking attor-neys. Answer choices C, D, and E are irrelevant to why the prestigious attorneys are not winning more cases. Answer choice B actually makes the situation even more paradoxical.

stimulus: Air pollution from a rural factory may have caused increased levels of carbon dioxide in the air, but the argument that the increased level of carbon dioxide is harming the local livestock is clearly without merit; the amount of carbon dioxide near the factory is, in fact, less than that found in cities like Los Angeles every day.
question: The argument is vulnerable to criticism because it

choices.A: uses generalizations about a class to draw conclusions about an individual entity in that class
choices.B: presupposes the very conclusion that it attempts to prove
choices.C: supports its conclusion by using two conflicting claims
choices.D: uses a fact to support a conclusion when that fact's relevance has yet to be deter-mined
choices.E: in fact, grants a concession that is fatal to the argument's conclusion

explanation: The best answer is D. This is a flaw question. Whether the animals or people in Los Angeles are or are not adversely affected by the amount of carbon dioxide in their areas has not been proven relevant to understanding if the livestock near this rural factory are being harmed by the increased carbon dioxide.

stimulus: Jackson City has outgrown its current fire station. The existing station cannot be expanded to fit the city's needs because of building code restrictions. Real estate in the area of the existing station is far more expensive than building space on the west side of the city. Since the price of a building is a considerable portion of the total cost, it would be more economical to move the fire station to the west side of the city.
question: Which of the following, if true, most seriously undermines the argument's conclusion?

choices.A: City residents have expressed approval of the plan to move the city's fire station to the west side of the city.
choices.B: The fire station, if moved to the west side of the city, will still have to conform with Jackson City's citywide sanitation requirements.
choices.C: If the fire station is moved to the west side of the city, insurance rates will skyrocket because the west side of the city has higher arson and vandalism rates.
choices.D: If the fire station is moved to the west side of the city, residents there will have to contend with increased noise and traffic.
choices.E: There is already an ample water supply to support the fire station on the west side of the city.

explanation: The best answer is C. This is a weaken question. The correct answer needs to give a reason why moving the fire station to the west side of the city might not be more economical. Answer choice C does this because if the increase in the cost of insurance is higher than the amount the city would be saving by moving to the west side, then the move might not be the most economical choice. Answer choices A and E do not weaken the conclusion, and they may actually strengthen it. Answer choices B and D are irrelevant to the issue of whether the move is economically sound.

stimulus: Until recently, the sole electric company in country Y was owned and operated by the government with notoriously poor customer service. Finally, increased pressure by the inter-national community forced country Y to allow private electric companies to operate in country Y. However, because government taxes on outside electric companies have made these companies largely uncompetitive in country Y, the government-owned electric company still has notoriously poor customer service.
question: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.A: Without the government taxes put on outside electric companies, these electric companies would provide better customer service.
choices.B: Excellent customer service is not always a prerequisite for a company to survive in country Y.
choices.C: The outside electric companies will no longer continue to serve country Y unless the government taxes are abolished.
choices.D: Government taxes on businesses in country Y always make businesses uncompetitive.
choices.E: Without the government taxes, the majority of the citizens of country Y would do business with the outside electric companies.

explanation: The best answer is B. This is a conclusion question. Since the government-owned-and-operated electric company is still in business with its poor customer service, it appears answer choice B must be true. Answer choice A is incorrect because, although it might be true that the outside electric companies would provide better company service, this does not haveto be true based on the statements in the paragraph.

stimulus: Even though Allison had plenty of time during the week to write her midterm paper, which is due tomorrow afternoon, she chose to procrasti-nate. Allison still has enough time to write the paper, but only if she manages to stay in the library all day. However, Allison's best friend is getting married this afternoon in another city, and Allison is supposed to serve as maid of honor. Therefore, because of her irresponsibility in not finishing her paper sooner, Allison will have to decide whether to attend her friend's wedding or to write her midterm paper.
question: The argument comes to its conclusion by

choices.A: showing that two events cannot both happen because a condition necessary for one of the events to occur is incompatible with making the other event occur
choices.B: pointing to specific evidence that shows that one particular event will occur in order to prove that an alternative event will also occur
choices.C: invoking pathos in the reader to demonstrate why choosing one alternative over another is necessary
choices.D: attempting to establish that one alternative is clearly the correct choice by pointing to evidence that suggests a prior commitment
choices.E: arguing that both alternatives cannot be achieved due to an unlucky coincidence rather than an oversight

explanation: The best answer is A. This is an assumption question. Allison can only finish her midterm paper if she stays in the library all day. Allison cannot attend her best friend's wedding if she has to stay in the library all day. So either Allison is going to go to the wedding and not finish her paper, or Allison is going to stay in the library all day and miss the wedding.

stimulus: The increase in the price of housing in city Y has been caused by a decline in the number of housing units available compared to the influx of new residents to city Y searching for housing. Nevertheless, the total number of available housing units is presently larger than it was last month.
question: If the statements above are true, which one of the following can be properly inferred?

choices.A: A lack of available housing will deter new people from living in city Y.
choices.B: The supply of available housing will continue to increase.
choices.C: The number of residents seeking housing has increased over the last month.
choices.D: The number of landlords leaving the housing market has increased this month.
choices.E: The cost of housing will continue to rise in proportion to demand.

explanation: The best answer is C. This is a method of argument question. If the total number of housing units is larger than last month, the only way the statements above are true is that the demand for housing has increased as well. Answer choice D is incorrect because this would probably not account for why more housing is avail-able this month than last.

stimulus:
Jill: State funding has been recommended to encourage the automobile industry to create vehicles that will better withstand collisions. Unless new vehicles are made that can better withstand collisions, highway safety cannot be improved. The automobile industry does not have the funds to conduct the research needed to produce vehicles that are better equipped to withstand collisions. Hence, without this state funding, the safety of drivers is compromised.

Mark: But collisions on our highways occur mainly because of drivers driving at excessive speeds, which will stop once the state increases highway patrol forces to catch speeders. Therefore, the state's highways will be safer even without the state funding this research for the automobile industry.
question: Which one of the following is an assumption on which Mark's argument depends?

choices.A: The increased presence of the highway patrol will not itself somehow cause more accidents than it prevents.
choices.B: The highway patrol could make better use of state funding to promote highway safety by hiring more officers rather than purchasing new radar equipment.
choices.C: The cost to install more highway patrol forces will be less than the amount of funding that would be given to the auto-mobile industry.
choices.D: Drivers realize that driving at excessive speeds is the main cause of collisions on highways.
choices.E: The state has the financial means to install more highway patrol forces and give funding to the automobile industry.

explanation: The best answer is A. This is an assumption question. If the increased amount of highway patrol will cause more accidents than it prevents, then the state's highways will not become safer like Mark claims. Answer choice C is incorrect because Mark's argument does not depend on it costing the state less to install more highway patrol. Rather, Mark's argument addresses the increased safety that will occur with more highway patrol.

stimulus:
Jill: State funding has been recommended to encourage the automobile industry to create vehicles that will better withstand collisions. Unless new vehicles are made that can better withstand collisions, highway safety cannot be improved. The automobile industry does not have the funds to conduct the research needed to produce vehicles that are better equipped to withstand collisions. Hence, without this state funding, the safety of drivers is compromised.

Mark: But collisions on our highways occur mainly because of drivers driving at excessive speeds, which will stop once the state increases highway patrol forces to catch speeders. Therefore, the state's highways will be safer even without the state funding this research for the automobile industry.
question: Mark uses which of the following argumentative techniques in countering Jill's argument?

choices.A: arguing that Jill's solution will not cure the problem, but rather postpone resolving the problem
choices.B: pointing out that Jill's conclusion leads to another set of even more drastic consequences
choices.C: showing that a fact used in Jill's argument is contradictory with another fact used to support her argument
choices.D: arguing that Jill's theory is correct, but not on the grounds that Jill uses to support it
choices.E: producing further claims that if true, weaken a premise in Jill's argument

explanation: The best answer is E. This is a method of argument question. Jill is claiming that without this state funding to the automobile industry, highway safety cannot be improved. Mark is pointing out that the state has another, even better, way to achieve highway safety by increasing the highway patrol.

stimulus: Economists have long explained the rapid economic growth in state P by pointing to state P's tourism industry, which attracts visitors to state P's sandy beaches and picturesque state parks. However, recent economic studies on state P show that the money brought in by tourists is far less than economists had originally thought and is not nearly enough to adequately explain the rapid economic growth of state P.
question: If the statements above are true, they provide the most support for which of the following state-ments?

choices.A: Other industries in state P bring more money into the state than the tourism industry.
choices.B: The tourism industry is not the only cause of state P's rapid economic growth.
choices.C: The rapid economic growth in state P is not as great as economists originally thought.
choices.D: The economic studies show that state P's tourism industry has a negative effect on state P's economic growth.
choices.E: State P's sandy beaches and picturesque state parks are not state P's only tourist attractions.

explanation: The best answer is B. This is a strengthen question. Economists were wrong for believing that state P's rapid economic growth could be solely attributed to the tourism industry because the tourism industry apparently does not bring in enough money to adequately explain state P's rapid economic growth. There is obviously something else, or several things, in addition to the tourism industry that is leading to state P's rapid economic growth. Answer choice A is incorrect because the para-graph does not imply that any other industry alone is bringing in more money than the tourism industry. Answer choice C is also incorrect because the paragraph tells us that state P is experiencing rapid economic growth, but the economists just do not know what is causing the growth. Answer choices D and E are unsupported by the statements in the paragraph.

stimulus: In country Y, the subsidies to charities are set by the nation's lawmakers. Since one of the lawmakers' chief duties is to handle the nation's finances prudently rather than irresponsibly, it was assumed that this method of deciding charitable subsidies would be fair. However, this method of deciding charitable subsidies is clearly flawed, as most of country Y's lawmakers are actually heads of charities themselves and command their salaries as heads of these charities based on government subsidies.
question: The argument made by the author of the para-graph is that the current method of deciding charitable subsidies might not be wise because

choices.A: many lawmakers are heads of charities only to receive salaries based on government subsidies
choices.B: the salaries of heads of charities should not be dictated by government subsidies
choices.C: many heads of charities are undeserving of higher salaries
choices.D: many lawmakers' opportunistic instincts might prevent them from handling the nation's finances prudently with respect to deciding charitable subsidies
choices.E: many lawmakers would forgo higher salaries as heads of charities rather than see the nation's finances handled imprudently

explanation: The best answer is D. This is a conclusion question. The author is arguing that the lawmakers might have an incentive to allocate more subsidies to charities than would be prudent because many of the lawmakers would benefit from giving more subsidies to charities. Answer choice A is incorrect because the author does not try to argue that the only reason lawmakers head charities is to receive salaries based on government subsidies. The author is just concerned about the lawmakers making decisions about government subsidies to charities when it looks like some of that money will flow back to the lawmakers.

stimulus: In country Y, the subsidies to charities are set by the nation's lawmakers. Since one of the lawmakers' chief duties is to handle the nation's finances prudently rather than irresponsibly, it was assumed that this method of deciding charitable subsidies would be fair. However, this method of deciding charitable subsidies is clearly flawed, as most of country Y's lawmakers are actually heads of charities themselves and command their salaries as heads of these charities based on government subsidies.
question: Which of the following is most susceptible to a line of criticism most similar to that used in the argument in the passage?

choices.A: selecting restaurant critics from an association of retired career chefs
choices.B: granting veto power over applicants for a vacant board seat to a member of that board
choices.C: allowing food manufacturers to set the penalties for food manufacturers who use substandard ingredients
choices.D: giving a group of workers collaborating on a project the power to decide what marketing plan will be implemented
choices.E: choosing a team captain based on nominations from other players

explanation: The best answer is C. This is a parallel question. The food manufacturers might be tempted to set small penalties for using substandard ingredients so that they could also use substandard ingredients and only face the small penalties that they established.

stimulus: Residents at a retirement community always play card games for two hours, starting at 3:00 p.m. every afternoon. Although it is clear that the resi-dents take pleasure in this activity, they never continue their games for longer than two hours. Caregivers assume that since card games require great concentration and strain on the elderly resi-dents' eyes, playing for more than two hours would give the residents headaches that would interfere with their ability to play bingo in the evenings.
question: Which of the following, if true, most seriously calls into question the caregivers' explanation?

choices.A: Playing bingo takes just as much concentration and causes equal strain on the eyes as card games.
choices.B: Most of the residents at the retirement community rank bingo at the top of their list of favorite activities.
choices.C: Elderly people often complain of headaches after focusing intently on television or computer screens.
choices.D: Experts have proven that playing card games has tremendous health benefits for elderly people.
choices.E: Residents at the retirement community are served dinner at 5:00 p.m. every evening.

explanation: The best answer is E. This is a weaken question. The caregivers have hypothe-sized that the reason the residents stop playing card games after two hours is because the residents do not want to have headaches that would prevent them from playing bingo in the evenings. If answer choice E is true, it could be that the resi-dents just stop playing card games after two hours because it is dinner time. Answer choice A is incorrect because it might actually strengthen the caregiver's argument because the residents might be trying to conserve their concentration and limit their eye strain so that they can play bingo without a headache.

stimulus:
Frank: The Internet has allowed everyone to obtain a vast amount of information on every topic imaginable.

Jerry: That is not true. Much of the informa-tion available online is false.
question: Jerry's response shows that he interprets Frank's statement to imply that

choices.A: all the information available on the Internet is true
choices.B: everyone has an equal opportunity to obtain information on the Internet
choices.C: everyone should use the Internet to obtain information
choices.D: other sources are more reliable than the Internet
choices.E: the majority of people do not use the Internet

explanation: The best answer is A. This is a point of contention question. Answer choice A correctly identifies what Jerry feels to be Frank's assumption, that all information one would gather from the Internet is true. The disputed point is whether or not the Internet has allowed people to obtain a vast amount of information on most topics; by refuting that statement, Jerry is admitting to what he feels is the assump-tion inherent in Frank's argument. The other answer choices are irrelevant to the stimulus.

stimulus: After the first bite, the Mystery Recipe Contest judge has detected cumin, red pepper flakes, and lemon grass in the winning dish. These season-ings have a tendency to be potent, producing distinct flavors. Since the quantity of any seasoning in a recipe depends directly on how potent that seasoning tastes in the dish, the judge has determined that the dish contains cumin, lemon grass, and red pepper flakes, in order of decreasing relative quantity.
question: The judge's argument relies on which of the following assumptions?

choices.A: The judge was unable to detect any other seasonings in the winning dish.
choices.B: The bite that the judge took was representative of the whole dish.
choices.C: Recipes that contain cumin generally contain other spices that are more potent.
choices.D: The winning dish contains at least one other seasoning ingredient besides cumin, lemon grass, and red pepper flakes.
choices.E: Cumin, lemon grass, and red pepper flakes together produce a special and distinct flavor that allowed the judge to detect their existence in the winning dish.

explanation: The best answer is B. This is an assumption question. If the judge had taken a bite that was not properly mixed or was just the topping of the dish, it is possible that she was misled about the actual quantity of each seasoning in the dish. Answer choice E is incorrect because the judge may have been able to taste the three seasonings separately not because the three together produced a special flavor. Also, the judge's determination does not rely on this statement being true.

question: Dennis will either purchase his mother's house and live in San Diego, or else he will move to Miami, but Dennis will not do either of these unless he gets married. Dennis's mother will let Dennis purchase her house only if she attends his wedding, but not otherwise. Therefore, Dennis will purchase his mother's house and live in San Diego only if his mother attends his wedding. Which one of the following, if assumed, allows the conclusion above to be properly drawn?

choices.A: Dennis will purchase his mother's house if his mother allows him to purchase the house.
choices.B: Dennis will get married only if he is able to purchase his mother's house.
choices.C: Dennis's mother will attend the wedding only if Dennis invites her.
choices.D: The reason Dennis wants to get married is so he can buy his mother's house.
choices.E: Dennis's mother would not let him move to Miami and buy her house too.

explanation: The best answer is A. This is an assumption question. Dennis is only going to purchase his mother's house if he gets married. If we assume Dennis will purchase his mother's house and not move to Miami if his mother allows him to purchase her house, then the conclusion that Dennis will purchase his mother's house and live in San Diego, only if Dennis's mother attends the wedding, can be properly drawn.

stimulus: If a meat thermometer is poked into a steak, the steak's temperature can be correctly assessed. Therefore, since Will does not have access to a meat thermometer, his steak's temperature cannot be correctly assessed. If the steak's temperature cannot be correctly assessed, that steak will be over- or undercooked. Therefore, Will's steak will be over- or undercooked.
question: Which of the following arguments contains an error of reasoning like the one in the argument above?

choices.A: If a dog is walked frequently, the dog will be healthy. Without health, a dog cannot be happy. Since Roger walks his dog frequently, his dog will be both healthy and happy.
choices.B: If dogs are not walked frequently, some-times they will be unhealthy. Unhealthiness can make a dog unhappy. Therefore, since Nina walks her dog frequently, her dog will be happy.
choices.C: If dogs are walked frequently, they will get plenty of exercise. Therefore, since Jackie does not walk her dog frequently, her dog will not get plenty of exercise. Dogs that do not get plenty of exercise will be unhealthy. Therefore, Jackie's dog will be unhealthy.
choices.D: If dogs are walked frequently, the dog will be healthy. Without exercise like walking, dogs will not be healthy. So, in order to have a healthy dog, Dee should walk his dog.
choices.E: If dogs are not walked frequently, the dog will not be healthy. Therefore, if Lee does not walk his dog frequently, his dog will not be healthy.

explanation: The best answer is C. This is a parallel question. The problem with both the example in the paragraph and answer choice C is that they assume there is only one way of being able to correctly assess the temperature of a steak (example in paragraph) and exercise a dog (answer choice C). The error in reasoning is that this is assumed without proof. For example, perhaps one can correctly assess the temperature of a steak by tasting it or by looking at it. If this is the case, Will's lack of a meat thermometer does not mean his steak will be over- or undercooked. Correspondingly, perhaps there are ways to make sure dogs get plenty of exercise besides walking them frequently. If so, Jackie's dog might not be unhealthy even though it does not get walked frequently.

stimulus:
Striking newspaper carrier: The fact that this subscriber canceled her newspaper subscription is a triumph for the striking workers. It shows that the subscriber supports the striking worker's claim that they are not getting paid enough.

Newspaper company X's president: That is ridicu-lous! The canceled subscription does not mean that the subscriber supports the striking workers. The subscription was canceled because the subscriber has said she does not read the news-paper every day and the subscriber prefers another newspaper. Therefore, the canceled subscription had nothing to do with supporting your strike.
question: The reasoning in newspaper company X's presi-dent's argument is flawed because the argument

choices.A: overlooks the possibility that the subscriber's proffered reasons for canceling her subscription may themselves show support for the striking workers
choices.B: fails to consider that any subscriber may wish to cancel his subscription in support of the striking workers
choices.C: tries to discount explicit evidence against its conclusion by diverting attention to an alleged flaw in his opponent's argument
choices.D: gives a detailed analogy to show how his opponent has mischaracterized the situation
choices.E: concedes a point made by an opponent that weakens the overall conclusion made by the company president

explanation: The best answer is A. This is a flaw question. Maybe the reason that the subscriber does not read the newspaper every day or the reason that she prefers another newspaper is because she does indeed support the striking worker's cause.

stimulus:
Striking newspaper carrier: The fact that this subscriber canceled her newspaper subscription is a triumph for the striking workers. It shows that the subscriber supports the striking worker's claim that they are not getting paid enough.

Newspaper company X's president: That is ridicu-lous! The canceled subscription does not mean that the subscriber supports the striking workers. The subscription was canceled because the subscriber has said she does not read the news-paper every day and the subscriber prefers another newspaper. Therefore, the canceled subscription had nothing to do with supporting your strike.
question: Which of the following, if true, most strongly supports the striking newspaper carrier's claim?

choices.A: The subscriber who canceled her subscription had previously written an editorial in a rival paper urging condemnation of newspaper company X's labor practices.
choices.B: The subscriber who canceled her subscription did not subscribe to any other news-paper.
choices.C: Most subscribers who canceled their subscriptions in support of the strike wrote letters explaining why they were canceling.
choices.D: Newspaper company X's president has recruited new subscribers because of the striking newspaper carriers.
choices.E: The subscriber who canceled her subscription did, in fact, read the newspaper most days.

explanation: The best answer is A. This is a strengthen question. If answer choice A were true, then this would be another piece of evidence to support the striking newspaper carrier's claim that the subscriber did cancel her subscription in support of the striking workers. Answer choice B is incorrect because the subscriber told news-paper company X's president that she preferred another newspaper, not that she intended to subscribe to another newspaper. This answer choice does not strengthen the striking newspaper carrier's claim.

stimulus:
Mortgage banker: There is a remarkable corre-lation between fluctuations in the federal interest rates and the strength of our nation's currency. Undoubtedly, despite the opinions of the majority of economists, the federal interest rates effectively control the strength of our nation's currency.

Economist: I beg to differ. Any experienced economist will testify that in regards to some-thing as complex as our nation's economic status, no consequential component is shaped or controlled by any one factor.
question: The renunciation by the economist of the banker's conclusion utilizes which one of the following techniques of argumentation?

choices.A: drawing an analogy to show the similarities between his opponent's argument and the economist's own conclusion
choices.B: challenging a conclusion regarding an explicit statement by appealing to an applicable principle
choices.C: offering a detailed counterexample that illustrates that a conclusion is incorrect
choices.D: forcing an opponent to elaborate on his facts in order to reveal a discrepancy
choices.E: showing that an opponent has purposefully excluded facts that are harmful to his argument

explanation: The best answer is B. This is a method of argument question. The economist denies the mortgage banker's conclusion by giving the general principle that no consequen-tial component of the nation's economic status is controlled by one factor.

stimulus: All of the athletes lined up in the park this after-noon were waiting to participate in a charity run. Blake, Tina, and Sara had all signed up to partici-pate in the charity run. No professional runners would sign up to participate in a charity run.
question: If the statements above are true, which of the following must also be true?

choices.A: Everyone in the park this afternoon was an amateur athlete.
choices.B: None of the athletes lined up in the park this afternoon had ever participated in a charity run.
choices.C: Neither Tina nor Sara is a professional runner.
choices.D: Blake, Tina, and Sara were the only athletes lined up in the park this afternoon.
choices.E: Blake, Tina, and Sara were not the only athletes lined up in the park this afternoon waiting to participate in a charity run.

explanation: The best answer is C. This is a conclusion question. The author tells the reader that no professional runners would sign up to participate in a charity run. Because Blake, Tina, and Sara were signed up to participate in the charity run, they could not be professional runners. Answer choice A is incorrect because there could have been professional runners in the park that afternoon who were not waiting to participate in the charity run.

stimulus: Insurance agent: Cars are no safer than motor-cycles; that is, when driven at high speeds, cars are not involved in more fatal crashes than are motorcycles. We conducted a survey about car Y and found that high-speed crashes involving car Y resulted in 40% of the fatalities in 2005 while motorcy-cles were involved in only 35% of the fatali-ties in 2005.
question: Each of the following describes a potential flaw in the insurance agent's reasoning EXCEPT:

choices.A: A conclusion is drawn about cars in general on the basis of a study focusing on car Y.
choices.B: The insurance agent based his conclusion on the total number of car crashes, not just on those resulting in fatalities.
choices.C: The survey being used to support the conclusion failed to take into account the significance of the total number of motor-cycles that are driven compared to the numbers of car Y that are driven.
choices.D: The insurance agent failed to consider how often motorcycles are driven at high speeds versus how often cars are driven at high speeds.
choices.E: The safety of a vehicle might depend on other factors besides how often that vehicle is involved in high-speed crashes resulting in fatalities.

explanation: The best answer is B. This is a conclusion question. The insurance agent's main point is that cars are no safer than motorcycles. Answer choices A, C, D, and E all highlight potential flaws in that argument. Answer choice B, which says the insur-ance agent's argument is based on the total number of car crashes, is not a flaw. This information would be a flaw in the argument if the argument were, indeed, premised upon it, but the insurance agent does not reference the total number of car crashes at any point, and this information is, therefore, irrelevant.

stimulus: During 2006, the number of applicants who applied to law school from college X tripled, even though the number of students who were declared pre-law majors stayed the same.
question: Which of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy above?

choices.A: During 2006, the career counselors at college X gave several presentations to the engineering and psychology departments about careers in law.
choices.B: During 2006, the local law schools around college X unanimously agreed to toughen admissions standards.
choices.C: During 2006, the number of applicants who applied to medical school from college X increased.
choices.D: During 2006, college X held several fundraisers to make an addition to the engineering building.
choices.E: Career counselors at college X have always supported students who wish to change their majors or areas of study.

explanation: The best answer is A. This is a paradox question. The correct answer is one that would help explain why more non–pre-law majors would apply to law school. Answer choice A helps to explain this. Answer choices B and E would contribute to the paradoxical situation. Answer choices C and D are irrelevant to why more non–pre-law majors applied to law school from college X.

stimulus: Since John Lindy was named vice president of sales, the highest ranked salespeople have been successfully recruited by rival companies, sales in all departments have plummeted, and company morale is down. This information clearly provides proof that John Lindy was named vice president of sales to ruin the company.
question: The reasoning in the argument is weak because the argument

choices.A: bases its conclusion on hearsay rather that hard evidence about the effect John Lindy has had on the company
choices.B: fails to show how company morale is related to sales plummeting in all departments
choices.C: argues that people are the highest ranked without giving proof of their achievement
choices.D: presupposes that because conditions resulted from a change, the change was made to create those conditions
choices.E: fails to show proof that the company has been ruined by John Lindy being named vice president of sales

explanation: The best answer is D. This is a flaw question. The paragraph tells us that after John Lindy was named vice president of sales, bad things started happening at the company. However, the facts given do not imply that John Lindy was purposefully named vice president to make these bad things happen. Therefore, that assumption is erroneous.

stimulus: Non-profit organizations have invested a great deal of money to build shelters for homeless people in large cities. However, not even one city has been able to build enough shelters for their homeless populations, and people are becoming homeless faster than shelters are being built. More of the money invested by non-profit organizations should be used in the future to prevent people from becoming homeless. Because preventing homelessness is more effi-cient than building shelters for homeless people, it is imprudent that the amount of money set aside for prevention of homelessness is less than the amount spent to build just one shelter.
question: The suggestion about how the non-profit organi-zations' money should be used in the future plays which of the following roles in the argument?

choices.A: It is the fact pattern on which the argument is based.
choices.B: It offers an objection to an additional suggestion mentioned in the argument.
choices.C: It both sustains the argument in the para-graph while supporting the opposing argument.
choices.D: It proposes an unsubstantiated objection to the current state of affairs.
choices.E: It is the claim that the argument as a whole is designed to sustain.

explanation: The best answer is E. This is a role of fact question. The argument's conclusion is that more of the non-profit organizations' money should be used to prevent people from becoming homeless. Therefore, the suggestion about how the money should be used is actually the conclusion that the whole paragraph is meant to support.

stimulus: Internet music downloading websites allow consumers to download music onto their home computers. Patrons of these music downloading websites purchase more albums from retail stores than people who do not download music through these websites. Therefore, downloading music on these websites actually encourages consumers to purchase more albums than they otherwise would.
question: The argument is most vulnerable to criticism because it

choices.A: fails to consider that the concurrent existence of two states of affairs does not imply that one caused the other
choices.B: suggests a premise must be false because of the lack of evidence to support it
choices.C: uses inherently self-contradicting claims to support its conclusion
choices.D: generalizes about the behavior of a large group based on the actions of a few unrepresentative samples
choices.E: takes a circumstance that by itself assures the occurrence of a desired result to be the only way the desired result can be obtained

explanation: The best answer is A. This is a flaw question. The fact that patrons of music downloading websites happen to buy more albums from retail stores does not mean that these music downloading websites actually encourage this behavior. It could just be coincidental.

stimulus: Based on studies by the state health department, the Surgeon General has formulated tables that list standard exercise requirements for various age groups. People whose activity level falls within the range given for their age experience fewer cardiovascular problems than those whose activity level falls below the given range. Therefore, if people whose activity level falls below their given range increased their time exercising to fall within that range, their cardio-vascular health would improve.
question: Which one of the following is an assumption on which the argument relies?

choices.A: The Surgeon General intended her table to help motivate people to increase their activity level and improve their cardiovascular health.
choices.B: Some individuals would be willing to increase their activity level solely to improve their cardiovascular health.
choices.C: Increasing the activity level would not itself cause cardiovascular health problems for people.
choices.D: People who follow the Surgeon General's table guidelines have better overall health than those who do not.
choices.E: The tables created by the Surgeon General take into account differences in metabolism and eating habits.

explanation: The best answer is C. This is an assumption question. The author of the para-graph is suggesting that people whose activity levels are within the preferred range will have improved cardiovascular health. If having an activity level within the range could, itself, actually cause cardiovascular health problems, then the author's argument fails. Answer choice A is incorrect because why the Surgeon General made her tables is irrelevant to the argument. Answer choice B is incorrect because the author's argument does not rely on the fact that people would be willing to increase their activity level. Answer choice D is incorrect because the argument does not claim that anything but cardiovascular health will be improved by following the Surgeon General's table. Answer choice E is incorrect because the author's argument does not rely on how the ranges were formulated. The author is just arguing that those whose activity level falls within the range have fewer cardio-vascular problems.

stimulus: Readers give more credibility and respond more positively to negative restaurant reviews if the critics begin their reviews by discussing the things they enjoyed about the restaurant. Studies show that readers enjoy hearing positive comments before being told unpleasant details. Therefore, any restaurant critic should make sure to start every review by giving ample praise about the positive aspects of the restaurant before launching into any negative commentary.
question: Which one of the following, if true, most seri-ously casts doubt on the wisdom of this recom-mendation?

choices.A: Most readers rarely take restaurant critics' advice about where to dine because they perceive the critics as being cynical and snobbish.
choices.B: Newspapers and magazines will often only publish the beginning of a restaurant review to save space.
choices.C: People usually decide which restaurants to patronize based on the negative comments made by restaurant critics.
choices.D: Restaurant critics often receive bribes from restaurants to write positive reviews.
choices.E: Most restaurant critics do not have any official culinary training or formal training in the food industry.

explanation: The best answer is B. This is a weaken question. If a critic is generally displeased with a restaurant, a newspaper or magazine that only publishes the beginning of the restaurant review will not show the overall impression that the critic had about the restaurant, and this would make the recommendation less wise. Answer choice C is incorrect because even by taking the author's suggestion to start with positive comments, the critic would still have the opportunity to write negative comments. Thus, people who decide which restaurants to patronize based on negative comments would still have a reason to read the review.

stimulus: One of the 10 computer manuals published by company T in 2005 was made for home computers. Exactly five of the advertisements released by company T featured those manuals written for home computers. Since 20 advertise-ments were released by company T in 2006, no more than one-quarter of them featured the computer manuals published by company T in 2005.
question: Which one of the following, if true, allows the conclusion above to be properly drawn?

choices.A: Some of the advertisements released by T in 2005 featured manuals made for home computers that were published in 2005.
choices.B: None of the graphics used in the advertisements released by company T in 2006 were done by professional artists.
choices.C: None of the advertisements released by company T in 2006 featured computer manuals other than the ones written for home computers.
